messages:
Alex Chen: Heads up — after rolling GPU drivers on the canary pool (550.7 -> 551.0) we’re seeing a 20-30% P95 regression on small-batch, short-seq workloads (batch<=4, seq<=512). perf-ci alerted this morning.
Maya Patel: which test/runner flagged it?
Alex Chen: perf/smoke/smallbatch-ec2-a100. Raw P95 tokens increased across the board. Repro script: `./perf/run_smallbatch.sh --driver 551.0 --reps 5`
perf-bot: perf-ci failed: smallbatch-ec2-a100 — p95 +24% (compare: baseline vs 551.0) — https://ci.internal/perf/2005X
Santiago Ruiz: do we have any NCU traces? this smells like a kernel choice flip (tiling or shared mem changes).
Alex Chen: grabbed a quick ncu snapshot — paste below.
```
== NCU SAMPLE ==
Kernel: matmul_v2_tiled
Avg time: 1.82 ms (old: matmul_fast 1.18 ms)
Shared mem spills: +42%\nSM occupancy: -10%\nL2 throughput: similar
```
Beth Park: interesting — matmul_v2_tiled is newer autotuned kernel we added in PR #2345 last week (autotune table refresh). Could be selector now preferring it for 32x32-ish tiles.
Maya Patel: timeline: driver bump was rolled by infra yesterday evening, then autotune table refresh merged in the same window. Which one is causal?
Santiago Ruiz: local bisect suggests kernel choice flip correlates with the autotune table change rather than the driver — the new table added a priority entry for shapes that occur in our small-batch path. But driver can change perf delta magnitude.
Alex Chen: ran quick revert of PR #2345 locally against driver 551.0 — matmul_fast restored as selected kernel and P95 returned to baseline within noise.
deploy-bot: canary rollback scheduled for next maintenance window if we confirm.
Ryan O'Neill: OK — that suggests the autotune table entry is the immediate trigger. Reverting seems safe, but we should avoid constant flipping on minor perf noise. Propose adding hysteresis to the kernel selector: require at least N=5 independent measurements and >10% improvement before flipping priority, and prefer older kernel for batch<=4 unless new kernel shows stable wins.
Santiago Ruiz: alternative: make selector aware of batch_size/seq combo and prefer legacy path for (batch<=4 && seq<=512). Also add a weighted score that factors in variance.
Beth Park: agree on both points. Also need an automated NCU capture step for perf-ci when p95 regresses so we can triage faster. Filed IR-789 with logs, ncu dump, and the bisect notes.
Alex Chen: action list: 1) revert PR #2345 on canary (hotfix branch) 2) add selector hysteresis + batch-aware preference (small patch) 3) add ncu-on-failure hook to perf-ci 4) follow-up to reconsider autotune defaults after more A/B testing.
Maya Patel: I'll open the hotfix PR and tag @oncall.
Alex Chen: thanks. Quick note — driver 551.0 amplifies the regression but isn't the root cause per local bisect. Keep infra in the loop in case they want to hold the driver roll.
Ryan O'Neill: cool. if revert fixes canary, we'll hold the table refresh until we have selector changes.
Beth Park: IR-789: https://issues.internal/IR-789 (includes snippets, stacktraces, and run commands).
Santiago Ruiz: leaving a small benchmark harness for the team: `python tools/bench_kernel_selector.py --shape 32 32 --batches 1 2 4 --reps 10`
Alex Chen: thx all :thumbsup:
thread_text_preview: Drivers + autotune table change caused small-batch P95 regression; bisect points to autotune table PR #2345; plan: revert + add selector hysteresis and ncu hook.
